requirement: Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.
rationale:
The two {test}-marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`. I read the `SEARCH_TEXT` branch of `impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[dispatch]` only to see where grouping and pagination happen. I took the expected behavior from the requirement text.

- **One entry per enclosing item, even with several hits:**
  - `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` searches `const B: &str = "hit hit";`. The raw `search_text` result has two hits for `code.rs#const[B]`.
  - The dispatched `search_text` page has exactly two entries (const A and const B), so const B's two hits collapse into one.
  - `search_pages_return_every_original_match_in_order` uses 350 lines of `hit {i} hit`, which is two hits per line. It asserts that each page entry equals the per-node, deduplicated expectation. The total count equals the number of lines.
- **Group before pagination, so an item's excerpt stays together:**
  - The implementation groups hits before calling `pages.search`.
  - The 350-line test asserts `pages > 1` and walks every page via `get_next_page`. Each entry must match `nodes[count]` and `lines[count]`, and the final count must equal `lines.len()`.
  - If pagination happened first, an item could be split or repeated across a page boundary. That would break the one-entry-per-node sequence or the final count.
- **Each entry carries a node reference, one excerpt, and a page-local tag:**
  - Both tests compare whole entries (`node`, `excerpt`, `tag`) with `assert_eq!`.
  - The pagination test checks that the tag is `index+1` on every page, so tags restart on each page.
  - The grouping test checks the excerpt for const B, which holds both hits and is a single string.
- **The tag accounts for use of the excerpt:** after `finish_search` with `used: []`, no dependencies are recorded. After it with `used: ["2"]`, exactly one `Dependency::Node` for const B is recorded, with the item's fingerprint.
- **The node reference lets the agent read the full item:** `session.read_node` on the returned entry yields a `Dependency::Node` for the same node.
- **The `node_reference` citation:** the entry's `node` is asserted equal to the serialized node of the hit, which is the integer form of `NodeId`. That requirement's own error behavior is not part of this subject.

I found no plausible violation of the requirement that these tests would accept, so I report no gaps.

text: Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent harness uses the unsigned integer representation of `NodeId<D>` for the current node, supplied inputs, and nodes in tool results. Built-in tools accepting a node ID resolve that integer in the domain's cache. A malformed value or an unassigned integer produces a tool error before any graph read.
For example, if a search hit contains `"node": 7`, the agent can call `read_node({"node": 7})` to read the enclosing node.
